title: Civil-Military Operations (CMO) Chief (MGySgt to Sgt) NMOS (1751, 1795), DC I
raw_text:
8. MOS 1739, Civil-Military Operations (CMO) Chief (MGySgt to Sgt) NMOS
(1751, 1795), DC I

    a. Summary. Civil-Military Operations Chiefs assist in the planning,
coordinating, and assessment civil affairs operations (CAO) and civil-
military operations (CMO). These Staff Noncommissioned Officers assist in
advising MAGTF commanders and their staff sections on the conduct of CMO as
well as in understanding and shaping civil conditions to support MAGTF
operations. CMO Chiefs assist with integrating CMO into the Marine Corps



                                         3-124                        Enclosure (1)
 3118                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



planning process (MCPP) across the range of military operations. CMO Chiefs
assist in the development of green cell products, and they coordinate, plan
and assist in the developing an Annex G supporting a MAGTF or joint task
force (JTF) operation plan or operations order.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must possess PMOS 1751, Influence Specialist.

            (2) Security requirement:     secret clearance eligibility.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Civil-Military Operations Planner Chief
Course (M02ZSED), Marine Corps Civil-Military Operations School (MCCMOS),
Quantico, VA.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to NAVMC
3500.124A, Information Maneuver Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Emergency Management Specialist 13-1061.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Civil Affairs Specialist, 1732.

            (2) Influence Specialist, 1751.

The Information Maneuver Occupational Field integrates information capability areas and the military occupational specialties (MOS) of cyberspace, space, electromagnetic warfare, civil affairs, and psychological operations into a single OCCFLD. Marines from these disciplines utilize their exquisite talents, knowledge, skills, and abilities to generate, preserve, and apply informational power against a relevant actor in order to increase or protect competitive advantage or combat power potential within all domains of the operating environment. Duty assignments include Marine Corps Forces Cyberspace Command, Marine Corps Forces Space Command, Marine Corps Information Command, Marine Cryptologic Support Battalion, Marine Corps Information Operations Center, MEF information groups, HQMC, MARFORs, joint organizations, and staff sections at all levels of the MAGTF.

8. MOS 1739, Civil-Military Operations (CMO) Chief (MGySgt to Sgt) NMOS (1751, 1795), DC I a. Summary. Civil-Military Operations Chiefs assist in the planning, coordinating, and assessment civil affairs operations (CAO) and civil- military operations (CMO). These Staff Noncommissioned Officers assist in advising MAGTF commanders and their staff sections on the conduct of CMO as well as in understanding and shaping civil conditions to support MAGTF operations. CMO Chiefs assist with integrating CMO into the Marine Corps planning process (MCPP) across the range of military operations. CMO Chiefs assist in the development of green cell products, and they coordinate, plan and assist in the developing an Annex G supporting a MAGTF or joint task force (JTF) operation plan or operations order. b. Prerequisites (1) Must possess PMOS 1751, Influence Specialist. (2) Security requirement: secret clearance eligibility. c. Requirements. Complete the Civil-Military Operations Planner Chief Course (M02ZSED), Marine Corps Civil-Military Operations School (MCCMOS), Quantico, VA. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to NAVMC 3500.124A, Information Maneuver Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
